column2: On your first day, an unexpected commotion breaks out in the middle of the hall. What do you do?
Restore order formally and calm the commotion.
First read why the commotion started and who stands to gain.
Rush to the front and throw yourself in.
Quietly watch everyone from a distance.
Gather people in one place and make a safe path.
A report comes in that a gate has opened near a village. Why do you go on the subjugation?
Because a gate is an evil that must be struck down.
I am curious about the gate's structure and the boss's identity.
I calculated that the reward and spoils outweigh the risk.
Because it is the best stage to raise my name.
I want to understand what effect it has on the surrounding ecology.
Which approach to magic class appeals to you most?
Formal magic, refined with elegance and precision.
Stable magic that many can use together for a long time.
Magic that twists fixed methods to test new uses.
Dazzling magic that no one can help but watch.
Overwhelming explosive power unleashed in an instant.
You and a colleague have a serious disagreement. How do you settle it?
Lead the conversation and steer things in my favor.
Settle it by citing academy rules and precedent.
Decide it in a duel and accept the result gracefully.
Quietly note the other's weak points and step back.
Leave and walk a forest path to calm down.
In the break between classes, where do you head?
Deep in the library, leafing through old records.
The training ground. I'm not satisfied until I break a sweat.
The banquet hall, moving among people and widening my connections.
The shopping street, checking prices and watching the haggling.
The common lounge, tidying scattered seats and supplies.
Which role do you most want in a team project?
The leader who guides everyone.
The intelligence officer who gathers data and secretly analyzes it.
The treasurer who manages supplies and schedules.
The presenter who delivers the results and draws every eye.
The experimenter who mixes new ingredients and tests them.
Whom do you admire most?
A knight who kept faith and fought to the end.
A diplomat who led negotiations with great powers on skill alone.
A spy who knew everything and left no name.
An alchemist who found a new principle while being called a heretic.
A hermit who guarded an ancient forest all their life.
In a moment of crisis, which words speak to you most?
The more dangerous, the more worthwhile.
Lose your decorum and you lose everything.
If the numbers don't add up, stepping back is courage too.
The truth must be dug out to the end.
Protecting the weak is the duty of the strong.
What do you most want to do after graduation?
Become a court master of ceremonies and uphold the nation's dignity.
Join a front-line subjugation party and fight at the very front.
Build a research institute and prove a principle no one knew.
Grow a trading company and hold the flow of the continent.
Take on work in the shadows at the intelligence bureau.
What is your ideal way to end the day?
Stroll a garden, listening for the wind and the presence of spirits.
Carefully record the day in ledgers and logs.
Take the curtain call on stage to applause.
Help a lagging classmate train, then clink cups with comrades.
Stay up all night with a document you cannot decipher.
Last recommendation —
There are no right answers, so choose as your heart leads.
